findings.summary: The caption calls the threshold 'the dashed line in the left panel', but in the rendered PNG the rule is a fine dotted line. A reader sent looking for dashes is directed at a mark that is not there.

The right panel's third group, 'plan documents doubled', shows only the blue this-change bar (1.08) where the other two groups show a grey/blue pair. A reader cannot tell from the figure whether the base revision was measured and omitted, or never measured; the caption does not say. The comparison the section makes is against the head's own as-prepared arm, so the absence is legitimate, but it is unexplained in the artifact.

The two panels use different y limits (left 0.0-3.0 in 0.5 steps, right 0.0-4.0 in 0.5 steps) for the same quantity, so a bar of equal height means a different memory in each panel. Every bar is value-labelled and each axis states GiB, so no number is lost, but a cross-panel glance at heights misleads.

rubric_items.contrast: pass: value labels and titles are near-black on white, tick labels and the threshold annotation are mid-grey on white and legible; no text is drawn over a bar fill.
rubric_items.data_ink: pass: solid grey and blue bar fills plus one dotted threshold rule carry the ink; there is no gradient, texture or shading.
rubric_items.decoration: pass: no grid, background fill, frame or styled theme; only the left and bottom spines are drawn.
rubric_items.label_collision: pass: nothing is clipped at the canvas edge; the threshold annotation's two lines sit one above and one below its dotted rule rather than through a glyph; no label overlaps another label, a bar, or the value it annotates, including the 4.19 label above the tallest bar clear of the panel title.
rubric_items.legibility: pass: both panel titles, both 'peak resident memory [GiB]' axis labels, all tick labels, the wrapped group names and every bar's value label read at a glance; the threshold annotation sits in clear space to the right of the left panel's bars. Caveat recorded as a non-blocking finding: the panels use different y limits (0-3.0 vs 0-4.0).
rubric_items.table_form: pass: the picture carries a magnitude comparison plus a bound (half the base peak) drawn across the left panel, which a table would not show against the base peak.

rubric_note: judged only from the rendered 1400x720 PNG attached to this review
